subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first Control UI slice, or require a broader daily/week calendar design before implementation proceeds?
rationale: The remaining work is a new Control UI product surface, not a broken existing contract, and the open linked PR implements only part of the broader requested calendar/timeline scope.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase and repair the linked PR, preserve current contracts, and accept a 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice while tracking or rejecting the broader day/week/editing scope.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers define the daily, weekly, stats, validation, and drag-and-drop editing behavior as one product design.

options.title: Decline Core Calendar View
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR after documenting that the current list/run-history UI is sufficient for core.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase and repair the linked PR, preserve current contracts, and accept a 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice while tracking or rejecting the broader day/week/editing scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is tied to the current Control UI page architecture that the open PR must now target.
